The hot syngas is cooled through heat exchange with other process streams and scrubbed with water to remove persistent impurities like particulates, ammonia, halides, and recalcitrant tars. Scrubber water is purged and treated continuously an on-site wastewater treatment facility. After heat recovery, the remaining low-quality heat in the flue gas from the catalyst regenerator is utilized for feedstock drying. 3.4 Area 400: Alcohol Synthesis Cooled low-pressure syngas enters a six-stage centrifugal compressor system where the pressure is increased to approximately 1,500 psi or 2,350 psi in the HighRG and HighAlc cases, respectively. The pressurized syngas is fed to the tube sides of two vertical tubular reactors (shell and tube type) operating in parallel. An Albemarle molybdenum sulfide-type mixed alcohol catalyst is packed within the tubes of the reactor, which is oriented in a down-flow configuration. Reactions at ~ 595°F convert a portion of the syngas to oxygenate and hydrocarbon products to mirror the compositions provided by West Biofuels in Section 2.1. Heat from the reactions is removed by steam generation in the shell side of the tubular reactor. The reactor effluent consisting of mixed alcohols, gaseous by-products (such as CO and methane), and unconverted 2 syngas is cooled through heat exchange with other process streams. As the reactor effluent cools, alcohols and water are condensed and sent to downstream separation and purification equipment. 19 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications. The West Biofuels syngas compositions at the alcohol synthesis reactor inlet were different from the NREL model. In order to avoid any extrapolation of mixed alcohols reactor behavior from experimental data, the syngas inlet from the gasifier was matched with the West Biofuels experimental data (Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2). The steps taken during this modification were: (1) carbon species were maintained at the same level as the NREL model but CO, CO , H , H O etc., were adjusted with manipulation of H 2 2 2 and O, (2) the heating value of the syngas inlet stream, after the adjustment of composition, was lower than the NREL model, and in order to account for the extra heat that would otherwise be evolved mostly at high temperatures at the gasifier, it was assumed that the heat could be used for steam generation and electricity production. 50 MMBtu of heat was left unused, that can account for unused or lost heat that is expected in any thermal process.
